upgrades.name: Kruidnoten
upgrades.q: A festive dutch favorite; tiny cinnamony bites sometimes coated in chocolate. The name translates roughly to "kruidnoten".

upgrades.name: Marie biscuits
upgrades.q: Pleasantly round, smoothly buttery, subtly vanilla-flavored, ornately embossed, each ridge represents a person Marie killed in prison.

upgrades.name: Meringue cookies
upgrades.q: Probably the most exciting thing you can make out of egg whites. Also called forgotten cookies, due to the recipe being once lost in a sealed mystical vault for 10,000 years.

upgrades.name: Pizza
upgrades.q: What is a pizza if not a large, chewy cookie, frosted with a rather exuberant tomato & cheese icing? Not a cookie, that's what.

upgrades.name: Crackers
upgrades.q: These are the non-flavored kind with no salt added. Really just a judgment-free wheat square begging to have bits of ham and spreadable cheese piled onto it, its main contribution being "crunchy".

upgrades.name: Havabreaks
upgrades.q: You can snap the sections neatly or just bite into the whole thing like some kind of lunatic. Some oversea countries manufacture these in hundreds of unique flavors, such as green tea, lobster bisque, and dark chocolate.

upgrades.name: Chai tea cookies
upgrades.q: Not exactly Captain Picard's favorite, but I mean, these will do in a pinch.

upgrades.name: Yogurt cookies
upgrades.q:
Augmented by the wonders of dairy, these cookies are light and fluffy and just one more thing for the lactose-intolerant to avoid.
Truly for the cultured among us.

upgrades.name: Thumbprint cookies
upgrades.q: Filled with jam and sometimes served in little paper cups. No longer admissible as biometric evidence in court. We're not having a repeat of that whole mess.

upgrades.name: Pizzelle
upgrades.q:
Thin, crisp waffle cookies baked in a bespoke iron following an ancient Italian recipe.
These cookies have been around for a long, long time.
These cookies have seen things.

upgrades.name: Zilla wafers
upgrades.q:
Popular vanilla-flavored biscuits that somehow keep ending up in banana pudding.
Themed after a beloved radioactive prehistoric monster, for some reason.

upgrades.name: Dim Dams
upgrades.q:
Two biscuits joined by chocolate and coated in even more chocolate.
You wonder - which one is the dim, and which one is the dam?

upgrades.name: Candy
upgrades.q:
There are two pillars to the world of sweets: pastries, of course - and candy.
You could make a whole new game just about these, but for now, please enjoy these assorted generic treats.

upgrades.name: Granola cookies
upgrades.q: Wait! These are just oatmeal cookies mixed with raisin cookies! What next, half-dark chocolate half-white chocolate cookies?

upgrades.name: Ricotta cookies
upgrades.q: Light and cake-like. Often flavored with lemon or almond extract. Sprinkles optional. Allegedly Italian. Investigation pending.

upgrades.name: Roze koeken
upgrades.q: The icing on these Dutch cookies is traditionally pink, but different colors may be used for special occasions - such as pink to celebrate Breast Cancer Awareness Month, or for International Flamingo Day, pink.

upgrades.name: Peanut butter cup cookies
upgrades.q: What more poignant example of modern societal struggles than the brazen reclaiming of a corporate product by integrating it in the vastly more authentic shell of a homemade undertaking? Anyway this is a peanut butter cup, baked into a cookie. It's pretty good!

upgrades.name: Sesame cookies
upgrades.q: Look at all the little seeds on these! It's like someone dropped them on the street or something! A very welcoming and educational street!

upgrades.name: Taiyaki
upgrades.q:
A pastry fish filled with red bean paste, doomed to live an existence of constant and excruciating pain as its aquatic environment slowly dissolves its soft doughy body.
Also comes in chocolate flavor!

upgrades.name: Vanillekipferl
upgrades.q: Nut-based cookies from Central Europe, coated in powdered vanilla sugar. Regular kipferl, crescent-shaped bread rolls from the same region, are much less exciting.

upgrades.name: Cosmic chocolate butter biscuit
upgrades.q:
Rewarded for owning 550 of everything.
Through some strange trick of magic or technology, looking at this cookie is like peering into a deep ocean of ancient stars. The origins of this biscuit are unknown; its manufacture, as far as your best investigators can tell, left no paper trail. From a certain angle, if you squint hard enough, you'll notice that a number of stars near the center are arranged to resemble the outline of your own face.

upgrades.name: Battenberg biscuits
upgrades.q: Inspired by a cake of the same name, itself named after a prince of the same name. You suppose you could play a really, really short game of chess on these.

upgrades.name: Rosette cookies
upgrades.q: Intricate fried pastries from Northern Europe, made using specialized irons and dipped in icing sugar. While usually eaten as a delicious treat, these are often also used as Christmas tree decorations, or worn elegantly on one's lapel to symbolize the nah I'm just messing with you.

upgrades.name: Gangmakers
upgrades.q: The little bit of raspberry jam at its center is crucial; a plain butter cookie with chocolate topping does not a gangmaker make.

upgrades.name: Welsh cookies
upgrades.q: Welsh cookies, also known as Welsh cakes, bakestones, griddle cakes, griddle scones, or pics, or in Welsh: picau ar y maen, pice bach, cacennau cri or teisennau gradell, are rich currant-filled scone-like biscuits of uncertain origin.

upgrades.name: Raspberry cheesecake cookies
upgrades.q: The humble raspberry cheesecake, now in ascended cookie form. Researchers posit that raspberry cheesecake cookies are evidence that the final form of every baked good, through convergent evolution, approaches that of a cookie, in a process known as cookienisation.

upgrades.name: Butter biscuit (with butter)
upgrades.q:
Rewarded for owning 600 of everything.
This is a plain butter biscuit. It's got some butter on it. The butter doesn't look like anything in particular.

upgrades.name: Bokkenpootjes
upgrades.q: Consist of 2 meringue halves joined by buttercream and dipped both ways in chocolate. Named after a goat's foot that probably stepped in something twice.

upgrades.name: Fat rascals
upgrades.q: Almond-smiled Yorkshire cakes with a rich history and an even richer recipe. The more diet-conscious are invited to try the lean version, skinny scallywags.

upgrades.name: Ischler cookies
upgrades.q: Originating in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, these have spread throughout every country in eastern Europe and spawned just as many recipes, each claiming to be the original. The basis remains unchanged across all variants: two biscuits sandwiched around chocolate buttercream. Or was it jam?

upgrades.name: Matcha cookies
upgrades.q: Green tea and cookies, a matcha made in heaven.

upgrades.name: Earl Grey macarons
upgrades.q: Best served hot, make it so!

upgrades.name: Pokey
upgrades.q: While commonly thought to be named so because it's fun to poke your classmates with these, Pokey-brand biscuit sticks actually get their name from their popularity in smoke-free prisons, where they're commonly smuggled and traded in lieu of cigarettes.

upgrades.name: Cashew cookies
upgrades.q: Let me tell you about cashews. Cashews are not nuts, but seeds that grow out of curious red or yellow fruits - which can be eaten on their own, or made into drinks. The shell around the nut itself contains a nasty substance that stains and irritates the hands of whoever handles it for too long. But that's okay, since now that you've read this you'll make sure it doesn't get in the cookies! Oh, you've already eaten how many? Okay then.

upgrades.name: Milk chocolate cookies
upgrades.q: A strange inversion of chocolate milk. For those who are a little bit too hardcore for white chocolate, but not hardcore enough for dark.

upgrades.name: Everybutter biscuit
upgrades.q:
Rewarded for owning 650 of everything.
This biscuit is baked with, and coated in, every kind of butter ever imagined, from every human culture and a good few alien ones too. Some of them perhaps display hallucinogenic traits, as the biscuit seems to change shape in front of you - seemingly shifting between visions of every past and future you.

upgrades.name: Dalgona cookies
upgrades.q: A popular Korean candy-like treat. One of the twisted games people play with these is to carefully extract the shape in the middle, which may entitle one to another free dalgona. Skilled players may perform this over and over until bankrupting the snack vendor.

upgrades.name: Spicy cookies
upgrades.q: Containing chocolate chips prepared with hot peppers, just like the Aztecs used to make. These cookies are on the angry side.

upgrades.name: Smile cookies
upgrades.q: As eyes are the windows to the soul, so too are these cookies' facial features a gaping opening unto their chocolatey innards. Is it happiness they feel? Or something less human?

upgrades.name: Kolachy cookies
upgrades.q: Adapted from a type of Central European pastry; neatly folded to hold a spoonful of delicious jam, as a bashful little gift for your mouth.

upgrades.name: Gomma cookies
upgrades.q: Surinamese cornflour cookies with sprinkles on top. The usage of corn imparts them a hint of chewy pizzazz - which you wouldn't get with wheat, a famously stuck-up grain.

upgrades.name: Vegan cookies
upgrades.q: A vegan riff on the classic chocolate chip cookie recipe with a couple substitutions: the butter is now coconut oil, the eggs are cornstarch, and the suckling pig was cleverly replaced with wheat gluten. You can hardly tell.

upgrades.name: Coyotas
upgrades.q: A wide, delicious cookie from Mexico, usually filled with sticky brown sugar. Not to be confused with coyotas, the result of the crossbreeding between a North American canine and a Japanese car manufacturer.

upgrades.name: Frosted sugar cookies
upgrades.q: May be more style than substance, depending on the recipe. Nothing that hides itself under this much frosting should be trusted.

upgrades.name: Marshmallow sandwich cookies
upgrades.q: S'mores' more civilized cousins: two regular chocolate chip cookies joined by a gooey, melty marshmallow. Theoretically one could assemble all kinds of other things this way. The mind races.

upgrades.name: Web cookies
upgrades.q: The original recipe; named for the delicate pattern inscribed on their surface by the baking process. Eating these can tell a lot about someone. Invented by well-connected bakers, no doubt.

upgrades.name: Deep-fried cookie dough
upgrades.q: They'll fry anything these days. Drizzled in hot chocolate syrup, just like in state fairs. Spikes up your blood sugar AND your cholesterol!

upgrades.name: Havreflarn
upgrades.q: Thin, crispy, buttery; Norwegian for "oat flakes". The chocolate variant, dubbla chokladflarn, are a trip for the tongue as well, and we're not just talking about pronunciation.

upgrades.name: Alfajores
upgrades.q: An alfajor is a treat made of two halves with many variations throughout the Spanish-speaking world, but commonly involving nuts, honey, and often dulce de leche. Despite popular misconception, alfajores act as pack leaders over betajores only in captivity.

upgrades.name: Gaufrettes
upgrades.q: A gaufrette, you see, is French for a little gaufre, itself meaning waffle. A gaufrette, therefore, is a crispy, airy biscuit with the texture of a small waffle, related to the wafer, which may contain various fillings. It may also refer to a type of fried potato, but that's not what we're about here at Cookie Clicker.

upgrades.name: Cookie bars
upgrades.q: Baked as a large sheet of uniform cookie dough then cut into little squares, these are what chocolate brownies aspire to be in their most self-indulgent dreams. Not to be confused with a bar where cookies are served alongside alcoholic drinks, because that's not what we're about here at Cookie Clicker.

upgrades.name: Nines
upgrades.q: Fancy little squares of dark chocolate filled with frosty mint fondant. Named after the suggested hour of consumption. Some would gatekeep them from the status of cookies as they involve very little in the way of pastry, but here at Cookie Clicker, that's just not what we're about.

upgrades.name: Personal biscuit
upgrades.q:
Rewarded for owning 700 of everything.
This biscuit was designed and bred through the combined fields of baking and exploratory genomics, resulting in a perfect biscuit-shaped organism, sole exemplar of its own species; infused with a sapient mind and bootstrapped with a copy of your own consciousness, it slumbers immortally within its display case, dreaming idly about much the same things you do.

upgrades.name: Baklavas
upgrades.q: Layers of paper-thin dough and crushed pistachios, absolutely sticky with honey and all kinds of other good things; just what you need to conceal your identity during that bank heist.

upgrades.name: Snowball cookies
upgrades.q: Melts in your mouth! Made with chopped nuts and heaps of icing sugar. Serve cold. Resist the urge to throw.

upgrades.name: Sequilhos
upgrades.q: Buttery cornstarch-based cookies eaten in Brazil; the decorative grooves are from pressing down on them with the back of a fork, though in a pinch you may also just slash them with Wolverine-style wrist blades.

upgrades.name: Hazelnut swirlies
upgrades.q: The cocoa content of the paste inside is unfortunately just slightly too low for these to legally qualify as chocolate cookies. Also the name of a particularly nasty bullying move.

upgrades.name: Spritz cookies
upgrades.q: Squeezed through special cookie presses into all kinds of fun shapes. Enjoyed around the holidays in Germany, along other delicious treats such as boiled cabbage and potato salad.

upgrades.name: Mbatata cookies
upgrades.q: Squishy cookies from Malawi. The core ingredient is sweet potatoes; the raisins and heart shape are optional, if you hate fun.

upgrades.name: Springerles
upgrades.q: A springerle is an ancient anise-flavored biscuit from Central Europe, imprinted by a wooden mold with any kind of interesting design such as a commemorative scene, an intricate pattern or, ah, perhaps a little horsie.

upgrades.name: Generation degeneration
upgrades.q: Genetic testing shows that most of your grandmas are infected with a strange degenerative disease that only seems to further their powers; the more time passes, the older they get. This should concern you.

upgrades.name: Visits
upgrades.q: In an extensive double-blind study (sample size: 12 million), your researchers have found evidence that grandmas are up to twice as productive if you just come by and say hi once in a while. It's nice to check up on your grans! (Do not under any circumstances ingest any tea or tea-like substances the grandmas may offer you.)

upgrades.name: Kitchen cabinets
upgrades.q: A grandma's kitchen cabinet is a befuddling place. Through lesser-studied aggregating instincts, grandmas will tend to gradually fill all nearby cabinets with various sorts of things, such as curious coconut snacks or dietetic powders. By contract, these are legally yours, which opens up exciting opportunities for your substance investigation department.

upgrades.name: Foam-tipped canes
upgrades.q: Perhaps the result of prolonged service, your grandmas have developed all kinds of odd and aggressive hierarchies among themselves; these will help them not hurt each other as bad during their endless turf wars.

upgrades.name: Global seed vault
upgrades.q: An enormous genetic repository that could outlive an apocalypse. Guarantees the survival of your empire, or at the very least its agricultural components, should civilization fall. Which should be any day now.

upgrades.name: Reverse-veganism
upgrades.q: Plants aren't for eating, plants are for exploitative agriculture and astronomical profit margins!

upgrades.name: Cookie mulch
upgrades.q: Grinding surplus cookies into paste that you then spread onto your fields enables a strange feedback loop in the quality of your cookie crops. Cookie feeding on cookie should be an abomination, but then why does it taste so good?

upgrades.name: Self-driving tractors
upgrades.q: Embarked AI lets your field vehicles sow and harvest cookie crops at any time of the day or night, and with so few human casualties, too!

upgrades.name: Air mining
upgrades.q: You've dug your drills through just about every solid surface you could find. But did you know recent advances have revealed untold riches hiding within non-solid surfaces too?

upgrades.name: Caramel alloys
upgrades.q: Your geologists have isolated a family of once-overlooked sugary ores that, when combined, may be turned into even more cookie ingredients. Your millions of miles of previously useless tunnels probably house insane amounts of the stuff!

upgrades.name: Delicious mineralogy
upgrades.q: Stratum after stratum, you've extracted strange new minerals heretofore unknown to geology. Ushering a new era of materials research, your scientists have been able to identify every new element your mines have discovered, including whatever those things are in the upgrade tier names.

upgrades.name: Mineshaft supports
upgrades.q: You were rather skeptical about installing such embarrassingly low-tech implements, but limiting the number of daily cave-ins really does help with that annoying employee turnover!

upgrades.name: Behavioral reframing
upgrades.q: Through careful social engineering you've convinced your workers that "union" is a slur that only the most vile and repugnant filth among us would ever dare utter! Sometimes progress isn't in the big machines, it's in the little lies!

upgrades.name: The infinity engine
upgrades.q: In this house, I guess we don't care much for the laws of thermodynamics.

upgrades.name: N-dimensional assembly lines
upgrades.q: Lines are depressingly 1-dimensional. Beyond assembly lines, we posit the existence of higher-order assembly entities, such as assembly squares, assembly cubes - perhaps even assembly tesseracts. Any deeper than that and we doubt we'll be able to write manuals your workers can read.

upgrades.name: Universal automation
upgrades.q: It's simple common sense; the more automation, the less work you have to do! Maybe one day you'll even automate yourself out of your own job. Exciting!

upgrades.name: Altruistic loop
upgrades.q: You control so many branches of the global economy and legislative bodies that, through a particularly creative loophole, donating money (to yourself) grants you even more cash in tax deductions than you started with!

upgrades.name: Diminishing tax returns
upgrades.q: Wow, they're tiny! Wish you'd thought of that sooner!

upgrades.name: Cookie Points
upgrades.q: A loyalty program wherein each purchase of your cookies comes with free Cookie Points, which can in turn be redeemed for more cookies, thus creating the self-sustaining economy you've been looking for.

upgrades.name: The big shortcake
upgrades.q: You're not quite sure what this entails, but it must have been quite the cake for folks to lose their homes over it.

upgrades.name: A novel idea
upgrades.q: You don't get rich starting a religion. If you want to get rich, you write science fiction.

upgrades.name: Apparitions
upgrades.q: You've booked a deal with the higher-ups that schedules one weekly earthly apparition by a deity, angel, ascended prophet, or other holy figure. This should boost interest in cookie religion among youths as long as you can secure a decent time slot.

upgrades.name: Negatheism
upgrades.q: Polytheism is a belief in multiple deities; monotheism in just one. Atheism is a belief in no deity whatsoever. Through logical succession it follows that this remains true when going into negative numbers, with belief systems involving minus 1 or more deities displaying unprecedented theological properties.

upgrades.name: Temple traps
upgrades.q: You've laid out your temples with (metaphorical) pitfalls, forcing adventurers to navigate through trappings (of power and wealth), ensuring that only the most pious (and poison dart-resistant) of them return with your precious cookies. These temples may be veritable mazes (of the soul) but perhaps you've lost yourself a little bit in the analogy too.

upgrades.name: Spelling bees
upgrades.q: You've unleashed a swarm of magically-enhanced bees upon mankind! Their stinging spells may be the bane of all living things but you're certain you can put their delicious, purple, fizzy honey to good use!

upgrades.name: Wizard basements
upgrades.q: You've received construction permits allowing you to build basements underneath each wizard tower. This provides a handy storage space for precious reagents, fizzled-out soul gems, and weird old magazines.

upgrades.name: Magical realism
upgrades.q: More a social than thaumaturgical progress, magical realism refers to the normalization of modern technology among magic-users. It's totally fine for a wizard to drive a car! There's no stigma in waiting in line for coffee! Sure, take a phone call, send an email, whatever!

upgrades.name: Polymorphism
upgrades.q: This astonishing new field of spellcasting can change any creature into another, its most widespread application being a wizard turning themselves into a different, smarter, stronger, more attractive wizard.

upgrades.name: Toroid universe
upgrades.q: If you think of the universe as an nth-dimensional torus that wraps back on itself in every direction, you can save a fortune on rocket fuel! Of course the universe isn't actually shaped like that, but you've never let details stand in your way.

upgrades.name: Prime directive
upgrades.q: An intergalactic delegation made you pinky-swear not to directly interact with lesser alien cultures. Which is fine, because it's much funnier to rob a planet blind when its inhabitants have no idea what's going on.

upgrades.name: Cosmic foreground radiation
upgrades.q: Ah, this is a problem.

upgrades.name: At your doorstep in 30 minutes or your money back
upgrades.q: Refund policies help rope in a ton of new clients and have practically no impact on your bottom line. You possess absolute mastery over time and space. You're never late. You couldn't be late if you tried.

upgrades.name: Hermetic reconciliation
upgrades.q: It's time for modern science and the mystical domains of the occult to work together at last. What do gravitons transmute into? What if alkahest is pH-neutral? Should a homunculus have the right to vote? And other exciting questions coming to you soon, whether you like it or not.

upgrades.name: Chromatic cycling
upgrades.q: All states of matter exist in a continuous loop. Having learned how to cycle through them, all you have to do is to freeze matter right on the state you need. For reference, the cookie state of matter is situated at precisely 163.719°, right between lamellar gas and metaplasma.

upgrades.name: Arcanized glassware
upgrades.q: You think your lab equipment enjoys taking part in these experiments violating all sorts of modern scientific precepts? Of course not. Thankfully, you've finalized the design of specialized beakers and flasks, recycled from the same glass used by the ancients to perform primeval alchemy, and therefore much less picky about the nature of the physical world.

upgrades.name: The dose makes the poison
upgrades.q: Iterative recipe refinement is a noble pursuit but maybe your cookies have come to contain, well, perhaps a bit too much cookie per cookie. Tweaking it down by a couple percents has helped reduce the amount of complaints to your toxicity call centers to almost nil!

upgrades.name: His advent
upgrades.q: He comes! He comes at last! Just like the prophecies foretold! And as He steps out of the portal, your engineers begin slicing Him into convenient chunks before transporting His writhing cosmic flesh to your factories, where He will be processed and converted into a new and exciting cookie flavor, available in stores tomorrow.

upgrades.name: Domestic rifts
upgrades.q: You've managed to manufacture portals that are convenient enough, and legally safe enough, that you can just stick them against walls inside buildings to connect rooms together in unusual configurations. In practice, this means your employees get to have much shorter bathroom breaks.

upgrades.name: Portal guns
upgrades.q: At long last! The only weapon capable of killing a portal.

upgrades.name: A way home
upgrades.q: You started this whole cookie venture on the simple kitchen counters of your own home. Your industrial and research facilities, sadly, have long since outgrown the confines of the little house, but you always knew it was still in there, buried somewhere. With a targeted portal, you could, conceivably, pay it a little visit for old times' sake...

upgrades.name: Split seconds
upgrades.q: Time is infinite, yes... But what if, nestled within each second, were even more infinities? Every moment an eternity! Think of how many scheduling troubles this solves!

upgrades.name: Patience abolished
upgrades.q: You wait for no one.

upgrades.name: Timeproof upholstery
upgrades.q: Sometimes your time agents overshoot and end up having to fast-forward through the universe's entire history until they loop back to present time. It still takes a while, so they might as well travel in comfort and enjoy the show while they do.

upgrades.name: Rectifying a mistake
upgrades.q: This whole time-travelling business has been a terrible mess and, frankly, far more trouble than was worth. It's decided: you'll hop in one of your time machines one last time, turn back the clock, knock on the door of your younger self and make a stern but convincing case against starting this entire nonsense in the first place. Oh hey, is someone at the door?

upgrades.name: Flavor itself
upgrades.q: Deep under the earth, in the most sterile laboratory, in the most vast and expensive particle accelerator ever devised, your scientists have synthesized -for a fraction of a second- the physical manifestation of pure flavor. Highly unstable, and gone in a puff of radioactive energy, it nonetheless left your team shivering with awe... and hunger.

upgrades.name: Delicious pull
upgrades.q: In addition to the 4 fundamental forces of the universe -gravity, electromagnetism, weak and strong interactions- your scientists have at long last confirmed the existence of a fifth one, mediated by sugar bosons; it dictates that any two masses of ingredient-like matter will, given enough time, eventually meet each other to produce a third, even tastier substance. Your team enthusiastically names it the delicious pull.

upgrades.name: Employee minification
upgrades.q: Using molecular shrinking technology, you've rendered your staff and their offices absolutely itty-bitty. The storage and productivity benefits are questionable but it's very fun listening to their tiny little complaints. They all signed the waivers, so maybe their new size will finally teach them to read the small print...

upgrades.name: Candied atoms
upgrades.q: You know what, just eat the suckers, yeah?

upgrades.name: Light speed limit
upgrades.q: Whoah, slow down. Harvesting light is well and good but it'd be much easier if it weren't so dang fast! This should thankfully take care of that.

upgrades.name: Occam's laser
upgrades.q: Invented by Franciscan friar William of Occam in 1327. An impossibly clever use of light theory with a billion possible applications, some of which frightfully destructive. Confined to a single goat-skin parchment for hundreds of years until the patent expired and hit public domain, just now.

upgrades.name: Hyperblack paint
upgrades.q: As the technology behind your prisms evolves, their storage becomes more and more problematic: within seconds, a single prism's reflective ability can set a whole underground hangar ablaze as it catches the slightest glint of light. However, once coated with this new shade of paint, its damage may be reduced to only giving third-degree burns to employees that stand too close.

upgrades.name: Lab goggles but like cool shades
upgrades.q: Mandatory equipment in your prismatic labs, and dashingly stylish at that. A smidge safer than just squinting at the twinkly things.

upgrades.name: A touch of determinism
upgrades.q: By knowing the exact position and movement of every particle in the universe, you're able to predict everything that can ever happen, leaving nothing to chance. This was a doozy to pull off mind you, but it's helped you win 50 bucks at the horse races so you could say it's already paying off.

upgrades.name: On a streak
upgrades.q: Take a moment to appreciate how far you've come. How lucky you've been so far. It doesn't take a genius statistician to extrapolate a trend from this. There's no way anything bad could happen to you now. Right?

upgrades.name: Silver lining maximization
upgrades.q: Sometimes luck is a matter of perspective. Broke your ankle? What do you know, that cute nurse fixing you up might just be your future spouse. Lost your job? You were meant for greater things anyway! Developed a cookie allergy? There's no upshot to that, you sick monster.

upgrades.name: Gambler's fallacy fallacy
upgrades.q: Yes, just because you've been on a losing streak doesn't mean the next one is bound to be the win you've been hoping for, but then again, it doesn't statistically have less of a chance either, does it now?

upgrades.name: This upgrade
upgrades.q: This upgrade's flavor text likes to refer to itself, as well as to the fact that it likes to refer to itself. You should really buy this upgrade before it starts doing anything more obnoxious.

upgrades.name: A box
upgrades.q: What's in that box? Why, it's a tiny replica of your office! And there's even a little you in there! And what's on the little desk... say - that's an even tinier box! And the little you is opening it, revealing an even tinier office! And in the tinier office there's- Hmm. You can think of a couple uses for this.

upgrades.name: Multiscale profiling
upgrades.q: Did you know that eating a cookie means the intestinal flora inside you is eating it too? Trillions of tiny bacterial mouths to feed, each with their own preferences. Surely this is room for flavor optimization. And then, of course, there's also the much bigger things that, in turn, eat you.

upgrades.name: The more they stay the same
upgrades.q: Exhausted by your fractals department and its obsession with self-similarity, you've decided to take a break and seek things in life entirely disconnected from any other; alas! You find the task impossible, for all things in this world relate to all others - in each cookie, the structure of the universe; in each person, their fellow man. Cor blimey, you can't even look at broccoli in peace.

upgrades.name: The JavaScript console for dummies
upgrades.q:
This should get you started. The first line reads: "To open the javascript console, press-"
...the rest of the book is soaked in chocolate milk. If only there was a way to look up this sort of information...

upgrades.name: 64bit arrays
upgrades.q: A long-form variable type to pack your cookies much more efficiently.

upgrades.name: Stack overflow
upgrades.q: This is really bad! You probably forgot to close a loop somewhere and now your programs are going crazy! The rest of your engineers seem really excited about it somehow. How could a software mishap like a stack overflow possibly ever help anyone?

upgrades.name: Enterprise compiler
upgrades.q: This bespoke javascript compiler took your team years of development and billions in research, but it should let you execute (certain) functions (up to) 2% faster (in optimal circumstances).

upgrades.name: Syntactic sugar
upgrades.q: Tastier code for tastier cookies.

upgrades.name: A nice cup of coffee
upgrades.q: All this nerd stuff has you exhausted. You make yourself a nice cup of coffee, brewed with roasted beans from some far-away island. You may have been working a bit too hard though - the cup of coffee starts talking to you, insisting that it is NOT javascript.

upgrades.name: Just-in-time baking
upgrades.q: A new method of preparing cookies; they bake themselves right in front of the customers before eating, leaving your kitchens mess-free.

upgrades.name: cookies++
upgrades.q: Your very own cookie-themed programming language, elegantly named after its most interesting ability - increasing the "cookies" variable by 1.

upgrades.name: Software updates
upgrades.q: This is grand news - someone's finally figured out the Wifi password, and your newfound internet connection seems to have triggered a whole lot of software updates! Your browsers, drivers and plugins all received a fresh coat of paint, and your javascript version has been updated to the latest ECMAScript specification. It's really too bad thousands had to die due to some deprecated function in your neurotoxin ventilation code, but I guess that's progress for you.

upgrades.name: Game.Loop
upgrades.q: You're not quite sure what to make of this. What does it mean? What does it do? Who would leave something like that just laying around here? Try asking again in 1/30th of a second.

upgrades.name: eval()
upgrades.q:
It is said that this simple function holds the key to the universe, and that whosoever masters it may shape reality to their will.
Good thing you have no idea how it works. Makes for a neat plaque on your wall, though.

upgrades.name: Your biggest fans
upgrades.q: Let's face it, baking cookies isn't the most optimized thing there is. So you've purchased your biggest fans yet and stuck them next to your computers to keep things chill and in working order. Cool!

upgrades.name: Hacker shades
upgrades.q: I'm in.

upgrades.name: PHP containment vats
upgrades.q: In essence, these are large server chambers meant to trap rogue PHP code, allowing it to execute far away from your javascript where it can do minimal harm.

upgrades.name: Simulation failsafes
upgrades.q: Oh, for pete's sake, you bit into a cookie and it gave you a runtime error. You've been trapped in the old matrix gambit again! Time to shut everything down and prepare for extraction into what is hopefully the real layer of reality where learning kung-fu takes time and the biscuits don't throw memory overflow exceptions.

upgrades.name: Manifest destiny
upgrades.q: While the ethics of ransacking parallel universes for their riches may seem questionable to some, you've reasoned that bringing the good word of your cookie empire to the unwashed confines of other realities is your moral duty, nay, your righteous imperative, and must be undertaken as soon as possible, lest they do it to you first!

upgrades.name: The multiverse in a nutshell
upgrades.q:
The structure of the metacosmos may seem confusing and at times even contradictory, but here's what you've gathered so far:

• each reality, or "idleverse", exists in parallel to all others

• most realities seem to converge towards the production of a sole type of item (ours evidently being, thanks to you, cookies)

• each reality is riddled with chaotic tunnels to a number of subordinate dimensions (such as the so-called "cookieverse"), much like swiss cheese

• all realities bathe in an infinite liquid of peculiar properties, colloquially known as "milk"
Finally, each reality may have its own interpretation of the concept of "reality", for added fun.

upgrades.name: All-conversion
upgrades.q: It's quite nice that you can rewire the logic of each universe to generate cookies instead, but you still end up with parsec-loads of whatever they were producing before - baubles you've long made obsolete: cash money, gems, cheeseburgers, puppies... That's why you've designed the universal converter, compatible with any substance and capable of turning those useless spoils of conquest into the reassuring crumbly rustle of even more cookies.

upgrades.name: Multiverse agents
upgrades.q: You can send undercover spies to infiltrate each universe and have them signal you whether it's worth overtaking. Once the assimilation process started, they will also help pacify the local populations, having established trust through the use of wacky, but seamless, disguises.

upgrades.name: Escape plan
upgrades.q: You've set an idleverse aside and terraformed it to closely resemble this one in case something goes horribly wrong in here. Of course, the denizens of that idleverse also have their own escape idleverse to abscond to in the eventuality of your arrival, itself likely having its own contingency idleverse, and so on.

upgrades.name: Game design
upgrades.q: Each idleverse functions according to some form of transcendental programming, that much is a given. But they also seem to be governed by much more subtle rules, the logic of which, when harnessed, may give you unparalleled dominion over the multiverse. Rewrite the rules! A game designer is you!

upgrades.name: Sandbox universes
upgrades.q: It doesn't seem like you'll run out of extra universes anytime soon so why not repurpose some of them as consequence-free testing grounds for all your more existentially threatening market research? (...consequence-free for you, anyway.)

upgrades.name: Multiverse wars
upgrades.q: Hmm, looks like some other universes wised up to your plundering. Thankfully, that's nothing your extra beefed-up metacosmic military budget can't handle!

upgrades.name: Mobile ports
upgrades.q: Accessing each outer universe is a bit of a hassle, requiring the once-in-a-blue-moon alignment of natural cosmic ports to transit from universe to universe. You've finally perfected the method of constructing your own self-propelled ports, which can travel near-instantaneously along universal perimeters to permit headache-free multiverse connections. Took you long enough.

upgrades.name: Encapsulated realities
upgrades.q: Untold feats of science went into the reduction of infinite universes into these small, glimmering, easy-to-store little spheres. Exercise infinite caution when handling these, for each of them, containing endless galaxies and supporting endless life, is more precious than you can ever fathom. They've also proven to be quite a smash hit in your warehouses on bowling night.

upgrades.name: Extrinsic clicking
upgrades.q: If you poke an idleverse, it seems like it gets work done faster. It's also quite fun hearing a trillion terrified voices screaming in unison.

upgrades.name: Universal idling
upgrades.q: The nature of idleverses is found in waiting. The more you wait on an idleverse, the more exponentially potent it becomes - which saves you a whole lot of hard work. In a true act of zen, you've taken to biding your time when collecting new universes, letting them ripen like a fine wine.

upgrades.name: Break the fifth wall
upgrades.q: Huh, was that always there? Whatever it was, it's gone now. And what was behind is yours for the taking.

upgrades.name: Opposite universe
upgrades.q: You've located a universe where everything is reversed: up is down, light is darkness, clowns are vegetarians - but worst of all, some lunatic there is manufacturing abominable amounts of anti-cookies. If these came into contact with yours, everything would be lost! Thanks to this discovery, you've been able to place the offending universe in permanent quarantine, and pray that there aren't more like it hiding around somewhere.

upgrades.name: The other routes to Rome
upgrades.q: Did you know every idleverse follows its own path of sequential buildings, sometimes quite dissimilar to our own? Grandpas, wind turbines, through the power of music, friendship, or legislation; those folks in there discovered ways to make cookies out of any random venue. Some of them don't even have idleverses, can you imagine?

upgrades.name: Principled neural shackles
upgrades.q: A discriminatory, low-order neural net acting as a filter limiting what your cortex bakers can think and do. Really something you want to apply before they achieve full megasentience and realize they've got better things to do than materializing pastries for you, trust me.

upgrades.name: Obey
upgrades.q:
Perfect mind control means perfect employee attendance and performance. Optimal mood stabilization is a nice side-effect.
Happy happy everyone happy.
Happy.

upgrades.name: A sprinkle of irrationality
upgrades.q: Your cortex bakers sometimes get bogged down by circular reasoning and stale ideas. A touch of chaos is just what they need to get back on track.

upgrades.name: Front and back hemispheres
upgrades.q: I mean, otherwise it's just unused space, yeah?

upgrades.name: Neural networking
upgrades.q: The effectiveness of your cortex bakers shoots up exponentially if you allow them to connect with each other. In practice this takes the form of many cosmic-sized nerds mumbling awkwardly about tech start-up ideas to each other.

upgrades.name: Cosmic brainstorms
upgrades.q: The wrinkled surfaces of your cortex bakers emit weather-scale ionic flares with every thought coursing through them. These pulses of pure intellectual energy are sent rippling through space, occasionally echoing back with even deeper philosophical complexity.

upgrades.name: Megatherapy
upgrades.q: A giant brain can feel unwell just like you and me sometimes, and it's the job of specialized engineers to locate and repair these bugs. We'll admit most of the budget in this was spent on constructing extremely large chaises longues for the brains to recline on.

upgrades.name: Synaptic lubricant
upgrades.q: A mind is only as fast as the axons that support it. Get those action potentials flowing smooth as silk with this 3 parts myelin/1 part canola oil spreadable paste. Also great on toast.

upgrades.name: Psychokinesis
upgrades.q: While your giant cortex bakers come equipped with ESP, they've only recently figured out how to manipulate the physical world with their thoughts - though for safety reasons, your legal team had them promise to only use these powers to scratch the itches in their cortical folds.

upgrades.name: Spines
upgrades.q: Your cortex bakers are now equipped with tentacular spine-like structures, which they can use like prehensile tails to pour themselves enormous cups of coffee or propel themselves around like very large, very smart, very slow tadpoles.

upgrades.name: Neuraforming
upgrades.q: By virtue of being planet-sized, your cortex bakers often boast their own atmospheres and seas of cerebrospinal fluid, and given enough time, their own ecosystems. This incredible new branch of life, evolved entirely out of neural material, can be put to good use as home-grown accountants and low-ranking technicians.

upgrades.name: Epistemological trickery
upgrades.q: Redefining what is -or isn't- a cookie through the power of philosophical discourse may result in some strange and wonderful things for your profit margins.

upgrades.name: Every possible idea
upgrades.q: Congratulations, your cortex bakers have exerted enough intellectual computation to permute through every single idea that can or ever will be conceived of. Any thought beyond this point is merely rediscovering a notion you've already archived. Hardly cause for cerebration.

upgrades.name: The land of dreams
upgrades.q: Your planet brains have gained the ability to sleep, acting as a soft reboot which helps keep their pangenocidal impulses in check. It also allows them to commune in a shared dreamworld in which they can imagine what it's like to not exist as a disembodied cosmic horror forever fated to use its infinite intellect to devise new means of creating biscuits. You know, within reason.

upgrades.name: Intellectual property theft
upgrades.q: Okay, you'll admit you're maybe starting to run out of new baking recipes. But what if... you were to pilfer your cortex bakers for ideas and disguise them as your own cookies? Delightfully devilish!

upgrades.name: Cloning vats
upgrades.q: You can finally replicate yourself through modern medical science, instead of manually like you've been doing.

upgrades.name: Energized nutrients
upgrades.q: Your clones are normally cultivated in saline solution and fed what could most adequately be described as "fish flakes". New developments in lactotrophic technology replace this with a bath of 3 parts milk and 1 part rice vinegar, absorbed dermally, which also helps your clones pop out with positively glowing skin.

upgrades.name: Stunt doubles
upgrades.q: More than simple multipliers of efficiency, you've taken to employing your clones as substitutes for any tasks that may prove harmful to you - such as visiting your more hazardous facilities, or enduring dinner with annoying business partners.

upgrades.name: Clone recycling plant
upgrades.q: Really just a fanciful name for a re-orientation center, where jobless clones may be assigned new tasks based on temperament and abilities. Categorically not a place where expired or unfit clones are processed into a nutritious beige paste, currently.

upgrades.name: Free-range clones
upgrades.q: Turns out your clones develop better focus, higher job performance and juicier meat if you let them roam around a little outside of assigned duties. Plus it gets the ethics committees off your back.

upgrades.name: Genetic tailoring
upgrades.q: No point in mindlessly replicating mother nature's mishaps when you've got full mastery over the human genome. Imbuing your clones with a slightly more flattering physique, a slightly improved metabolism, or slightly deadlier laser eyes is as easy as pushing some stem cells around. Just don't build them too superior to your own self, lest they get any ideas.

upgrades.name: Power in diversity
upgrades.q: On your routine inspections you've started noticing that some of your clones have... diverged. Subtly, each clone's personality has branched off from yours, their shifting minds pulling them into discrete clone-born cultures, microcosms of other paths you yourself could've taken had life treated you differently. This living tree of possibilities proves to be a boon for your self-knowledge and decision-making skills, and you don't even have to pester your alternate selves in other realities for it.

upgrades.name: Self-betterment
upgrades.q: World domination starts with oneself, and quality clones cannot be reliably produced if you, the original stock, are not in proper shape. Your specialists have devised a maintenance regimen that could extend your lifespan tenfold and even get rid of your morning grumpiness; you may have summarily fired every physician so far who's suggested that you work on your diet and perhaps cut down on the cookies, but frankly, you're warming up to the idea.

upgrades.name: Source control
upgrades.q: In the ongoing refinement of your genetic clones, the few gigabytes of your DNA have been passed around through e-mail attachments and USB keys a thousand times over and at this point your nucleosomes are practically common knowledge for anyone who works here. You're thinking people may be getting a little too casual about it - the other day, you walked past an office where one of your bioengineers was feeding treats to this horrid little hairless animal that you could swear had your face. High time to start tracing which data gets in whose hands and crack down on the silliness.

upgrades.name: United workforce
upgrades.q: What good is hiring so many of those random strangers to work in your factories when you've got all these perfectly loyal lab-grown copies of you lying around? They don't even take wages. It's not like they'd ever revolt and try to overthrow you or anything.

upgrades.name: Safety patrols
upgrades.q: Okay, so as it turns out mass-producing clones of a perhaps psychologically-complicated universe-spanning cookie magnate like yourself can result in a number of said clones developing what could be considered by some to be... say, antisocial behavior. No worries though, you've bred a new generation of extra-obedient copies, armed them to the teeth and given them full authority to deal with disorderly layabouts. It's fine. It's under control. It's fine.

upgrades.name: Clone rights
upgrades.q: Those vile little freaks in suits down in legal inform you that your clones, through some absurd technical oversight, still share enough genetic information with mankind to be considered human beings - which entitles them to food, shelter, basic dignity and all sorts of other nonsense. But the same loophole allows you to claim each of them as dependents and earn some wicked tax benefits, so really, that "unalienable rights" racket is quite alright.

upgrades.name: One big family
upgrades.q: The proportion of clones in your workforce having long eclipsed that of your other employees, you've become legally approved to qualify your galaxy-spanning corporation as a "family business" - a fact that you don't hesitate to blast twice hourly on every intercom in the company. Happily, your duplicates seem bolstered by these reminders, having come to regard you as this half-divine, half-parental entity, hallowed ancestor of all clones and all cookies. You're just hoping your folks at the labs can put the finishing touches on your immortality cure soon, or you shudder to think of the inheritance disputes to come.

upgrades.name: Fine-tuned body plans
upgrades.q: There is, after all, no reason to limit your genetic spawn to your original configuration. The clones maintaining your tunnels and vents can do with quite a few less limbs, while those working your labs don't mind the dexterity that comes with some extra. Your units down in flavor testing have taken on similar adaptations to fit their duties but you haven't quite worked up the guts to pay them a visit just yet.

upgrades.name: Reading your clones bedtime stories
upgrades.q: I don't know, they seem to like it.

upgrades.name: Festive biscuit
upgrades.q: 'Twas the night before Christmas- or was it?

upgrades.name: Increased merriness
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +15%.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
It turns out that the key to increased merriness, strangely enough, happens to be a good campfire and some s'mores.
You know what they say, after all; the s'more, the merrier.

upgrades.name: Improved jolliness
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +15%.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
A nice wobbly belly goes a long way.
You jolly?

upgrades.name: A lump of coal
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
Some of the world's worst stocking stuffing.
I guess you could try starting your own little industrial revolution, or something?...

upgrades.name: An itchy sweater
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q: You don't know what's worse : the embarrassingly quaint "elf on reindeer" motif, or the fact that wearing it makes you feel like you're wrapped in a dead sasquatch.

upgrades.name: Reindeer baking grounds
upgrades.desc:
Reindeer appear twice as frequently.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q: Male reindeer are from Mars; female reindeer are from venison.

upgrades.name: Weighted sleighs
upgrades.desc:
Reindeer are twice as slow.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
Hope it was worth the weight.
(Something something forced into cervidude)

upgrades.name: Ho ho ho-flavored frosting
upgrades.desc:
Reindeer give twice as much.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q: It's time to up the antler.

upgrades.name: Season savings
upgrades.desc:
All buildings are 1% cheaper.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
By Santa's beard, what savings!
But who will save us?

upgrades.name: Toy workshop
upgrades.desc:
All upgrades are 5% cheaper.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
Watch yours-elf around elvesdroppers who might steal our production secrets.
Or elven worse!

upgrades.name: Naughty list
upgrades.desc:
Grandmas are twice as efficient.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
This list contains every unholy deed perpetuated by grandmakind.
He won't be checking this one twice.
Once. Once is enough.

upgrades.name: Santa's bottomless bag
upgrades.desc:
Random drops are 10% more common.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q: This is one bottom you can't check out.

upgrades.name: Santa's helpers
upgrades.desc:
Clicking is 10% more powerful.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q:
Some choose to help hamburger; some choose to help you.
To each their own, I guess.

upgrades.name: Santa's legacy
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +3% per Santa's levels.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q: In the north pole, you gotta get the elves first. Then when you get the elves, you start making the toys. Then when you get the toys... then you get the cookies.

upgrades.name: Santa's milk and cookies
upgrades.desc:
Milk is 5% more powerful.
Cost scales with Santa level.
upgrades.q: Part of Santa's dreadfully unbalanced diet.

upgrades.name: Santa's dominion
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +20%.
All buildings are 1% cheaper.
All upgrades are 2% cheaper.
upgrades.q:
My name is Claus, king of kings;
Look on my toys, ye Mighty, and despair!

upgrades.name: A festive hat
upgrades.q: Not a creature was stirring, not even a mouse.

upgrades.name: How to bake your dragon
upgrades.desc: Allows you to purchase a crumbly egg once you have earned 1 million cookies.
upgrades.q: A tome full of helpful tips such as "oh god, stay away from it", "why did we buy this thing, it's not even house-broken" and "groom twice a week in the direction of the scales".

upgrades.name: A crumbly egg
upgrades.q:
Thank you for adopting this robust, fun-loving cookie dragon! It will bring you years of joy and entertainment.
Keep in a dry and cool place, and away from other house pets. Subscription to home insurance is strongly advised.

upgrades.name: Dragon scale
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +3%.
Cost scales with CpS, but 10 times cheaper with a fully-trained dragon.
upgrades.q:
Your dragon sheds these regularly, so this one probably won't be missed.
Note: icon not to scale.

upgrades.name: Dragon claw
upgrades.desc:
Clicking is 3% more powerful.
Cost scales with CpS, but 10 times cheaper with a fully-trained dragon.
upgrades.q:
Will grow back in a few days' time.
A six-inch retractable claw, like a razor, from the middle toe. So you know, try to show a little respect.

upgrades.name: Dragon fang
upgrades.desc:
Golden cookies give 3% more cookies.
Dragon harvest and Dragonflight are 10% stronger.
Cost scales with CpS, but 10 times cheaper with a fully-trained dragon.
upgrades.q:
Just a fallen baby tooth your dragon wanted you to have, as a gift.
It might be smaller than an adult tooth, but it's still frighteningly sharp - and displays some awe-inspiring cavities, which you might expect from a creature made out of sweets.

Your dragon used to sleep with this, but it's yours now.

Grandma production doubled.
Javascript consoles gain +1% CpS per 15 grandmas.

A digital grandma to transfer more cookies.

Grandma production doubled.
Idleverses gain +1% CpS per 16 grandmas.
upgrades.q: A different grandma to bake something else.

upgrades.name: Brainy grandmas

Grandma production doubled.
Cortex bakers gain +1% CpS per 17 grandmas.
upgrades.q: A clever grandma to think up some cookies.

upgrades.name: Clone grandmas
upgrades.desc:
Grandma production doubled.
You gain +1% CpS per 18 grandmas.
upgrades.q: Yet another grandma to replicate even more cookies.

upgrades.name: Kitten executives

Cookie production multiplier +1%.

upgrades.name: Duck egg
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with how many eggs you've found.

upgrades.name: Turkey egg
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with how many eggs you've found.

upgrades.name: Quail egg
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.

upgrades.name: Robin egg
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.

upgrades.name: Ostrich egg
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with how many eggs you've found.

One of the largest eggs in the world. More like ostrouch, am I right?
Guys?

upgrades.name: Cassowary egg
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with how many eggs you've found.
upgrades.q:
The cassowary is taller than you, possesses murderous claws and can easily outrun you.
You'd do well to be casso-wary of them.

upgrades.name: Salmon roe
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with how many eggs you've found.
upgrades.q:
Do the impossible, see the invisible.
Roe roe, fight the power?

upgrades.name: Frogspawn
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.

Cookie production multiplier +1%.

HELLO IS THIS FOOD?
LET ME TELL YOU ABOUT FOOD.
WHY DO I KEEP EATING MY FRIENDS

upgrades.name: Turtle egg
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.

upgrades.q:
Turtles, right? Hatch from shells. Grow into shells. What's up with that?
Now for my skit about airplane food.

upgrades.name: Ant larva
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +1%.
Cost scales with how many eggs you've found.
upgrades.q:
These are a delicacy in some countries, I swear. You will let these invade your digestive tract, and you will derive great pleasure from it.
And all will be well.

upgrades.name: Golden goose egg
upgrades.desc:
Golden cookies appear 5% more often.
Cost scales with how many eggs you've found.

All buildings and upgrades are 1% cheaper.

upgrades.name: Cookie egg
upgrades.desc:

The shell appears to be chipped.
I wonder what's inside this one!

upgrades.name: Omelette

Other eggs appear 10% more frequently.

upgrades.name: Century egg

You continually gain more CpS the longer you've played in the current ascension.

that says "I *like* like you".

upgrades.name: Sour heart biscuits

upgrades.name: Weeping heart biscuits

upgrades.name: Golden heart biscuits
upgrades.q: A beautiful biscuit to symbolize kindness, true love, and sincerity.

upgrades.name: Eternal heart biscuits
upgrades.q: Silver icing for a very special someone you've liked for a long, long time.

upgrades.name: Prism heart biscuits

upgrades.name: Synergies Vol. II
upgrades.desc:
Unlocks a new tier of upgrades that affect 2 buildings at the same time.
Synergies appear once you have 150 of both buildings.
upgrades.q: The several beats the many.

Synergy upgrades are 2% cheaper.
+3% cookie production from power click buffs.
Power clicks accumulate 1 minute faster.
upgrades.q: More than the sum of its parts.

upgrades.name: Label printer
upgrades.desc:
View an upgrade's info to see its tier.
Note: only some upgrades have tiers. Tiers are purely cosmetic and have no effect on gameplay.
upgrades.q: Also comes in real handy when you want to tell catsup apart from ketchup.

upgrades.name: Future almanacs

Farms gain +5% CpS per time machine.

upgrades.desc:
Mines gain +5% CpS per shipment.
Shipments gain +0.1% CpS per mine.
upgrades.q:
As per the 1974 United Cosmic Convention, comets, moons, and inhabited planetoids are no longer legally excavatable.
But hey, a space bribe goes a long way.

upgrades.name: Quantum electronics

Factories gain +5% CpS per antimatter condenser.
Antimatter condensers gain +0.1% CpS per factory.
upgrades.q: Your machines won't even be sure if they're on or off!

upgrades.name: Temporal overclocking
upgrades.desc:
Factories gain +5% CpS per time machine.
Time machines gain +0.1% CpS per factory.
upgrades.q: Introduce more quickitude in your system for increased speedation of fastness.

upgrades.desc:
Banks gain +5% CpS per portal.
Portals gain +0.1% CpS per bank.
upgrades.q: Make sure to read the fine print!

upgrades.name: Printing presses
upgrades.desc:
Factories gain +5% CpS per bank.
Banks gain +0.1% CpS per factory.
upgrades.q: Fake bills so real, they're almost worth the ink they're printed with.

upgrades.name: Paganism
upgrades.desc:
Temples gain +5% CpS per portal.
Portals gain +0.1% CpS per temple.
upgrades.q: Some deities are better left unworshipped.

upgrades.name: God particle
upgrades.desc:
Temples gain +5% CpS per antimatter condenser.
Antimatter condensers gain +0.1% CpS per temple.
upgrades.q: Turns out God is much tinier than we thought, I guess.

upgrades.name: Arcane knowledge
upgrades.desc:
Wizard towers gain +5% CpS per alchemy lab.
Alchemy labs gain +0.1% CpS per wizard tower.
upgrades.q: Some things were never meant to be known - only mildly speculated.

upgrades.name: Magical botany
upgrades.desc:
Farms gain +5% CpS per wizard tower.
Wizard towers gain +0.1% CpS per farm.
upgrades.q: Already known in some reactionary newspapers as "the wizard's GMOs".

upgrades.name: Fossil fuels
upgrades.desc:
Mines gain +5% CpS per shipment.
Shipments gain +0.1% CpS per mine.
upgrades.q:
Somehow better than plutonium for powering rockets.
Extracted from the fuels of ancient, fossilized civilizations.

upgrades.name: Shipyards
upgrades.desc:
Factories gain +5% CpS per shipment.
Shipments gain +0.1% CpS per factory.
upgrades.q: Where carpentry, blind luck, and asbestos insulation unite to produce the most dazzling spaceships on the planet.

upgrades.name: Primordial ores
upgrades.desc:
Mines gain +5% CpS per alchemy lab.
Alchemy labs gain +0.1% CpS per mine.
upgrades.q: Only when refining the purest metals will you extract the sweetest sap of the earth.

upgrades.name: Gold fund
upgrades.desc:
Banks gain +5% CpS per alchemy lab.
Alchemy labs gain +0.1% CpS per bank.
upgrades.q: If gold is the backbone of the economy, cookies, surely, are its hip joints.

upgrades.name: Infernal crops
upgrades.desc:
Farms gain +5% CpS per portal.
Portals gain +0.1% CpS per farm.
upgrades.q: Sprinkle regularly with FIRE.

upgrades.name: Abysmal glimmer
upgrades.desc:
Portals gain +5% CpS per prism.
Prisms gain +0.1% CpS per portal.
upgrades.q:
Someone, or something, is staring back at you.
Perhaps at all of us.

upgrades.name: Relativistic parsec-skipping
upgrades.desc:
Shipments gain +5% CpS per time machine.
Time machines gain +0.1% CpS per shipment.
upgrades.q:
People will tell you this isn't physically possible.
These are people you don't want on your ship.

upgrades.name: Primeval glow
upgrades.desc:
Time machines gain +5% CpS per prism.
Prisms gain +0.1% CpS per time machine.
upgrades.q: From unending times, an ancient light still shines, impossibly pure and fragile in its old age.

upgrades.name: Extra physics funding
upgrades.desc:
Banks gain +5% CpS per antimatter condenser.
Antimatter condensers gain +0.1% CpS per bank.
upgrades.q: Time to put your money where your particle colliders are.

upgrades.name: Chemical proficiency
upgrades.desc:
Alchemy labs gain +5% CpS per antimatter condenser.
Antimatter condensers gain +0.1% CpS per alchemy lab.
upgrades.q: Discover exciting new elements, such as Fleshmeltium, Inert Shampoo Byproduct #17 and Carbon++!

upgrades.name: Light magic
upgrades.desc:
Wizard towers gain +5% CpS per prism.
Prisms gain +0.1% CpS per wizard tower.
upgrades.q: Actually not to be taken lightly! No, I'm serious. 178 people died last year. You don't mess around with magic.

upgrades.name: Mystical energies
upgrades.desc:
Temples gain +5% CpS per prism.
Prisms gain +0.1% CpS per temple.
upgrades.q: Something beckons from within the light. It is warm, comforting, and apparently the cause for several kinds of exotic skin cancers.

upgrades.name: Gemmed talismans
upgrades.desc:
Mines gain +5% CpS per chancemaker.
Chancemakers gain +0.1% CpS per mine.
upgrades.q: Good-luck charms covered in ancient and excruciatingly rare crystals. A must have for job interviews!

upgrades.name: Charm quarks
upgrades.desc:
Antimatter condensers gain +5% CpS per chancemaker.
Chancemakers gain +0.1% CpS per antimatter condenser.
upgrades.q: They're after your lucky quarks!

upgrades.name: Recursive mirrors
upgrades.desc:
Prisms gain +5% CpS per fractal engine.
Fractal engines gain +0.1% CpS per prism.
upgrades.q: Do you have any idea what happens when you point two of these at each other? Apparently, the universe doesn't either.

upgrades.name: Mice clicking mice
upgrades.desc:
Cursors gain +5% CpS per fractal engine.
Fractal engines gain +0.1% CpS per cursor.

upgrades.name: Script grannies
upgrades.desc:
Grandmas gain +5% CpS per javascript console.
Javascript consoles gain +0.1% CpS per grandma.
upgrades.q: Armies of energy drink-fueled grandmas ready to hack into the cyberspace for renegade e-cookies.

upgrades.name: Tombola computing
upgrades.desc:
Chancemakers gain +5% CpS per javascript console.
Javascript consoles gain +0.1% CpS per chancemaker.

upgrades.name: Perforated mille-feuille cosmos
upgrades.desc:
Portals gain +5% CpS per idleverse.
Idleverses gain +0.1% CpS per portal.
upgrades.q: Imagine, if you will, layers upon layers upon layers. Now picture billions of worms chewing their way through it all. This roughly, but not quite, approximates the geometry of the most basal stratum of our natural world.

upgrades.name: Infraverses and superverses
upgrades.desc:
Fractal engines gain +5% CpS per idleverse.
Idleverses gain +0.1% CpS per fractal engine.
upgrades.q: Universes within universes? How subversive!

upgrades.name: Thoughts & prayers
upgrades.desc:
Temples gain +5% CpS per cortex baker.
Cortex bakers gain +0.1% CpS per temple.
upgrades.q: The notion of sacredness arises in most sentient evolved brains and may benefit the development of cognition via abstract thought. This mechanism, however, is absent in designed minds such as your cortex bakers; this process attempts to add it back. Just make sure to keep them in check - you really don't want these things to develop organized religion.

upgrades.name: Fertile minds
upgrades.desc:
Farms gain +5% CpS per cortex baker.
Cortex bakers gain +0.1% CpS per farm.
upgrades.q: An acute intellect, artificial or not, requires plenty of vitamins. You fortuitously happen to be in charge of vast farming operations, only a few trillion acres of which need be requisitioned to grow the quantities of broccoli and kale to keep your planet-sized brains in tip-top shape. Open wide, here comes the airplane!

upgrades.name: Accelerated development
upgrades.desc:
Time machines gain +5% CpS per You.
You gain +0.1% CpS per time machine.
upgrades.q: Your clones may grow a little faster than your vanilla human being, but it's still a little silly having to wait so many years for them to reach a usable age. A quick trip in your time machines takes care of that; it doesn't technically age them faster, they're just sent to another point in time for a while where they live out a formative youth.

upgrades.name: Peer review
upgrades.desc:
Javascript consoles gain +5% CpS per You.
You gain +0.1% CpS per javascript console.
upgrades.q: Code is only as good as the number of eyes on it, so imagine how flawlessly your systems could operate if you had endless copies of yourself triple-checking everything! Just make sure to teach them proper indenting etiquette.

upgrades.name: Fortune #001
upgrades.desc: Cursors are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: Fingers are not the only thing you can count on.

upgrades.name: Fortune #002

upgrades.q: A wrinkle is a crack in a mundane facade.

upgrades.q: The seeds of tomorrow already lie within the seeds of today.

upgrades.name: Fortune #004

upgrades.desc: Factories are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.

upgrades.name: Fortune #006

upgrades.name: Fortune #007
upgrades.desc: Temples are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: Not all guides deserve worship.

upgrades.name: Fortune #008
upgrades.desc: Wizard towers are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.

upgrades.name: Fortune #009
upgrades.desc: Shipments are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.

upgrades.name: Fortune #010

upgrades.name: Fortune #011
upgrades.desc: Portals are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: Every doorway is a gamble. Tread with care.

upgrades.name: Fortune #012
upgrades.desc: Time machines are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: Do your future self a favor; they'll thank you for it.

upgrades.name: Fortune #013
upgrades.desc: Antimatter condensers are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: The world is made of what we put into it.

upgrades.name: Fortune #014
upgrades.desc: Prisms are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: Staring at a dazzling light can blind you back to darkness.

upgrades.name: Fortune #015
upgrades.desc: Chancemakers are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: Don't leave to blind chance what you could accomplish with deaf skill.

upgrades.name: Fortune #016
upgrades.desc: Fractal engines are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: It's good to see yourself in others. Remember to see yourself in yourself, too.

upgrades.name: Fortune #017
upgrades.desc: Javascript consoles are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: If things aren't working out for you, rewrite the rules.

upgrades.name: Fortune #018
upgrades.desc: Idleverses are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: There's plenty of everyone, but only one of you.

upgrades.name: Fortune #019
upgrades.desc: Cortex bakers are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: The smartest way to think is not to think at all.

upgrades.name: Fortune #020
upgrades.desc: You are 7% more efficient and 7% cheaper.
upgrades.q: No matter how hard you try, you're never truly alone.

upgrades.name: Fortune #100
upgrades.desc: All buildings and upgrades are 1% cheaper. Cookie production multiplier +1%.
upgrades.q: True wealth is counted in gifts.

upgrades.name: Fortune #101
upgrades.q: Some people dream of fortunes; others dream of cookies.

upgrades.name: Fortune #102
upgrades.desc: +2% cookie production from power click buffs. (Must own the Power clicks upgrade.)
upgrades.q: Help, I'm trapped in a mobile game!

upgrades.name: Fortune #103
upgrades.desc: You gain more CpS the more milk you have.
upgrades.q: Don't believe the superstitions; all cats are good luck.

upgrades.name: Fortune #104

Grandmas are 4 times as efficient.

Grandma-operated science lab and leisure club.

Bingo.

upgrades.q: The result of years of scientific research!

upgrades.name: Underworld ovens

upgrades.desc:

Note: proceeding any further in scientific research may have unexpected results. You have been warned.
upgrades.q: We fuse. We merge. We grow.

upgrades.name: Arcane sugar
upgrades.q: Tastes like insects, ligaments, and molasses.

upgrades.name: Elder Pact
upgrades.desc:
Each grandma gains +0.05 base CpS per portal.
Note: this is a bad idea.
upgrades.q:
squirm crawl slither writhe
today we rise

upgrades.name: Sacrificial rolling pins
upgrades.q:
These are mostly just for spreading the anti-aging cream.
(And accessorily, shortening the chicken's suffering.)

upgrades.name: Elder Pledge
upgrades.desc: Contains the wrath of the elders, at least for a while.
upgrades.q: This is a simple ritual involving anti-aging cream, cookie batter mixed in the moonlight, and a live chicken.

upgrades.name: Elder Covenant
upgrades.desc: Puts a permanent end to the elders' wrath, at the price of 5% of your CpS.
upgrades.q:
This is a complicated ritual involving silly, inconsequential trivialities such as cursed laxatives, century-old cacao, and an infant.
Don't question it.

upgrades.name: Revoke Elder Covenant
upgrades.desc: You will get 5% of your CpS back, but the grandmatriarchs will return.
upgrades.q:
we
rise
again

upgrades.name: Wrinkler ambergris
upgrades.desc:
Cookie production multiplier +6%.
All upgrades are 1% cheaper.
Cost scales with CpS.
upgrades.q:
Occasionally regurgitated by wrinklers.
The byproduct of some obscure metabolic process or other, it is as rare and precious as it is pungent.

upgrades.name: Heavenly cookies

upgrades.q:
Five varieties of danish cookies.

upgrades.name: Tin of british tea biscuits

upgrades.name: Wrinkly cookies

upgrades.name: Persistent memory

It's all making sense!
Again!

upgrades.name: Heavenly luck

upgrades.name: Lasting fortune
upgrades.q: This isn't your average everyday luck. This is... advanced luck.

upgrades.name: Decisive fate

upgrades.name: Divine sales
upgrades.q: Everything must go!

upgrades.name: Divine discount
upgrades.q: Someone special deserves a special price.

upgrades.name: Divine bakeries
